WITH cte_joined AS (
  SELECT 
    ab.abhvreg,
    t.tradekind
  FROM advancedbehavior ab
  INNER JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg
  INNER JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
),
cte_by_type AS (
  SELECT 
    tradekind,
    COUNT(*) as count_records,
    COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cte_joined) as share
  FROM cte_joined
  GROUP BY tradekind
),
cte_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(count_records) as avg_count FROM cte_by_type
)
SELECT 
  SUM(ct.count_records) as combined_number,
  AVG(ct.share) as average_share,
  AVG(ct.count_records - ca.avg_count) as average_above_avg
FROM cte_by_type ct
CROSS JOIN cte_avg ca
WHERE ct.count_records > ca.avg_count;

assumptions.assumption: "analysed trade records" refers to individual advancedbehavior records. Each advancedbehavior record is counted separately; if multiple such records reference the same transaction, both are counted.

alternatives.interpretation: Count each distinct transaction once per trader type, rather than counting each advancedbehavior record separately. Use DISTINCT tr.transreg in cte_joined to ensure transactions are counted only once, even if they have multiple linked advancedbehavior records.
